source.title: Straight to Zero: Why Linearly Decaying the Learning Rate to Zero Works Best for LLMs
source.authors: Shane Bergsma; Nolan Dey; Gurpreet Gosal; Gavia Gray; Daria Soboleva; Joel Hestness

record.tranche_reason: The paper fits power laws to validation loss versus compute for LLMs, using a different experimental setup and focusing on learning-rate schedules.
record.gate_note: The paper's main learning-rate schedule comparisons are not rows because they do not test the claim versions. Appendix C.11 reports two fitted loss-to-FLOPs power laws, one for each schedule; cited findings from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly about learning-rate schedules. Its Appendix C.11 fits loss-to-FLOPs power laws to four Llama-style models (272M–2.75B, 20 TPP, Pile validation) under two schedules, so its results bear weakly on V1. The exponent difference between schedules bears on V7. The power-law form is imposed rather than tested, and no fit quality or uncertainty is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that linear decay-to-zero is the best AdamW LLM schedule at compute-optimal and higher TPP, with gains growing with TPP. Its loss-to-FLOPs fit has a steeper slope, implying a growing gap: about 1% at 1.3B–2.7B and a projected about 2% at 70B, with no 70B run.
record.recipe_differences: The paper fits validation loss against compute across four Llama-style model sizes at fixed 20 TPP and compares learning-rate schedules; it does not reproduce the original studies' broader scaling-law or compute-optimal allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted loss-to-FLOPs slope differs between 10× and D2Z schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: The loss advantage of linear decay-to-zero over 10× decay grows with tokens-per-parameter, model size, smaller batch, and weight sparsity (Figures 6, 11, 13, 23).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedule effects on loss interact with training duration and scale, so schedule is a confounder in scaling-law comparisons.

record.problems: The scaling-law comparison covers four model sizes and a limited compute range; no uncertainty for the fitted exponents is reported, and the 70B projection is not checked against an actual run.

untested.parts: Separate loss laws in parameters or tokens with the other quantity not a bottleneck. Ranges of several orders of magnitude; the fit covers about one to two orders of compute. Goodness of fit against other functional forms.
Parameter counting, fitting method, data choices, compute-optimal split, and curvature away from a single power law.
The 70B projection is never checked against an actual run.
No allocation sweep; TPP is fixed at 20.
Shape is not compared at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated data, or fine-tuning scaling.
Downstream results (Table 5) compare schedules at one size and are not scaling fits.

missing.what: Per-size relative loss improvement of D2Z over 10× in the scaling sweep. It rises from about 0.4% to about 1.2% across 272M–2.75B.
Validation loss vs TPP (2–200) at fixed sizes of 111M, 610M and 1.7B for both schedules. It shows diminishing returns with tokens, but no power-law fit is given and model size is a bottleneck.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling-law part is a small appendix exercise. Four model sizes, single fits per schedule, no confidence intervals. The power law is imposed via log-log least squares. Evidence for V1 is therefore weak and evidence for V7 is a small, unquantified exponent shift. The relation could reasonably be judged uses_without_test for V1. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests loss against compute at fixed 20 TPP, not separate loss laws against parameter count or token count with the other quantities varied independently. The tested model and compute ranges are narrower than several orders of magnitude.
The paper projects a fit to 70B parameters but does not report an actual larger run against which that projection can be checked.
Does not measure the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation as compute changes.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests text pretraining with different training configurations, not other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer power laws.
Reports downstream evaluations for some schedule comparisons, but does not test whether downstream performance scales predictably with model scale or pretraining loss.

Shows a fitted exponent difference between two learning-rate schedules, but does not compare parameter-counting or fitting methods, test compute-optimal allocation exponents, or show curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: Llama-style models (aggregate scaling-law fit across 272M, 653M, 1.39B, and 2.75B models)
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss as a power law of pretraining FLOPs using least-squares linear regression in log space.

conditions.value: English, Arabic, and source code mix

rows.note: Aggregate fit over the four stated model sizes; the paper reports that the D2Z slope is roughly 2.5% better than the 10× slope.
rows.check: This row is the 10× schedule's own fitted law. It bears on V1: loss falls with compute along the imposed power law. Alone it cannot show V7's schedule dependence; that comparison belongs to r2. Figure 26's x-axis spans roughly 1e20–1e21 FLOPs, about one order of magnitude.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.11, Table 6 and Figure 26, pp. 29–30.

rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss as a power law of pretraining FLOPs using least-squares linear regression in log space.

rows.note: Aggregate fit over the four stated model sizes; the authors say the steeper fitted slope implies a growing performance gap at larger sizes.
rows.check: For V1 the D2Z fit behaves like r1 (observed). For V7 the schedule changes the exponent only from -0.0593 to -0.0608, about 2.5% relative. No uncertainty is given and the fit uses only four points, so the schedule dependence is small and of unclear significance. Partial reflects the V7 reading.

source_check.correct: V1: observed within the fitted sweep. V7: observed schedule dependence of the fitted exponent, from -0.0593 to -0.0608. V7 specifies no minimum magnitude of dependence.
source_check.problem: The small exponent difference does not establish incomplete expression of V7; the fitted exponent changes with schedule as V7 predicts.

statements.correction: 10× exponent: -0.0593; D2Z exponent: -0.0608; slope-magnitude difference: roughly 2.5%; four model sizes: 272M, 653M, 1.39B, 2.75B; training: 20 TPP; exponent uncertainty: not reported; direction: supports schedule dependence.
